name: Shipping chokepoints
summary: An ADNOC vessel was attacked in Hormuz on 17 Nov, with one missing and 11 injured; Hormuz traffic remains impeded
state: ADNOC Logistics & Services said one of its vessels was attacked in the Strait of Hormuz on the night of 17 Nov; one crew member is missing and 11 were wounded (The National, 18 Nov). UKMTO reported a tanker disabled near Oman on 17 Nov with its engine room on fire and all crew safe, the fourth attack in 24 hours; Iran's Guards claim tankers sank, which is unverified (NewsBytes). Hormuz traffic remains materially impeded.
for_you: Disruption at Hormuz raises shipping and insurance costs and can delay goods. Follow FCDO travel advice for the Gulf region.
rubric_hit: Hormuz traffic materially impeded by repeated attacks on shipping = Alert

sources.title: The National — Iran attacks Kuwait in widening escalation
NewsBytes — Tanker disabled in Strait of Hormuz, Iranian navy confirms
Arab News — Kuwait, Bahrain fend off Iranian aerial attacks

why: Around 30% of seaborne oil and much container trade passes Hormuz, Bab el-Mandeb/Suez, Panama and Malacca; disruption raises prices worldwide.
drivers: Houthi/Iran attacks, war-risk insurance, drought (Panama), naval incidents, piracy.

rubric.alert: Hormuz traffic materially impeded, or any chokepoint closed, or two or more disrupted at once.
rubric.watch: One chokepoint disrupted (attacks, large-scale diversions, draught restrictions).
